correctness.rationale: The interval multiplication equations are complete. The three endpoint-sensitive local solution counts are derived by enumerating exactly the three allowed middle diagonal states. In the zero-zero endpoint regime, finite-field additive-character orthogonality gives the separate nontrivial Fourier transform; other endpoint regimes contribute one linear equation in two variables. The resulting four exponential bases are strictly ordered for every finite-field order, so the recurrence has minimal order four. Independent left-multiplication rank enumeration exhaustively matches fourteen field-width cases, including extension field F4. Infinite validity follows from the explicit argument rather than experiments.

value.rationale: The finite-algebra one-sided zero-product relation is a natural multiplication invariant. Diamond incidence algebras are the smallest three-level ordinal-sum family in which a top interval receives contributions from every intermediate two-step path. A uniform four-exponential formula, the provably minimal fourth-order recurrence, and its exact growth constant solve an unbounded family over every finite-field extension, including characteristic two. This provides a reproducible benchmark for multiplication-fiber counting and is not simply the previously known outward-star case.
